reasons: F01, F04, F05, F06, F07, F16, F17, F18, F19: no material weakness, no going-concern doubt, no auditor change or disagreement, no prior-period correction, and no SEC, government or litigation activity. None of the usual governance or regulatory warning signs are present.
F14, F15, F11, F25, F28: management is stable (no CEO/CFO change, no interim CFO), there are no material related-party transactions, and there are no voluntary accounting or segment changes.
R08, R10, R19: total accruals and RSST accruals are about zero, and operating cash flow roughly equals net income (1.03), so earnings are backed by cash.

F08, F09, F10, F12, F13, F27: none of the higher-risk revenue features (over-time recognition, contract assets, return rights or bill-and-hold), and no significant inventory writedowns. This fits a simple finance or real-estate entity.
F21, R16: securities were issued and a capital raise happened or is planned in the year. This gives some incentive to present results favourably, which raises risk modestly.
R13: soft assets are 89% of total assets, which is high, though normal for a finance, insurance or real-estate holder of financial assets. It points to valuation judgement risk.

F03, R01-R07, R09, R17: the company is not required to have an ICFR auditor attestation (a smaller filer), and most Beneish and Dechow inputs are n/a. That limits the screening coverage, but nothing that could be computed is anomalous.
